Improve Delivery Efficiency and Reduce Operating Costs

Thematic Area: Delivery Intelligence & Operational Productivity

How might we identify and improve the delivery activities that create the greatest avoidable costs while maintaining reliable service?

Background

A delivery business wants to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs. It is seeking technology partners to identify practical improvements across delivery operations.

The opportunity is to target a measurable operating bottleneck and improve delivery performance. Route planning, service coverage and hub placement are key applications for exploration.

Relevant startups work in logistics software, geospatial analysis, routing and operational analytics. The collaboration will define the workflow, operating constraints and performance measures for a focused trial.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Higher delivery costs: Avoidable travel, waiting time and poor coordination increase operating expenses.
  • Limited productivity: Operational bottlenecks restrict the number of deliveries completed with available resources.
  • Slower expansion: Delivery growth depends on resolving bottlenecks while maintaining service reliability.

Existing Efforts

  • Available capabilities: A geospatial platform provides location, traffic, route and heatmap analysis for reviewing delivery coverage, route conditions and hub locations. A university routing prototype tested in eldercare transport offers a research foundation for freight-specific adaptation.
  • Collaboration focus: Select an operating bottleneck, establish current performance and connect relevant location and delivery data. Run a focused trial comparing cost per delivery, travel time, lateness and resource utilisation.

Potential Market Size

  • Global route optimisation software market: The global market is estimated at US$12.2 billion in 2026 and is forecast to reach US$21.5 billion by 2030, reflecting demand for routing technology across transport applications.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
